payload.description:
Launch article for Chatticus. Keep unpublished until Chatticus launches.

Working title: Chatticus: The AI Organization You Control

Core thesis:
- Grok Bot proved that named, persistent, collaborating bots on a shared computer can feel like an organization instead of a collection of chat sessions.
- OpenClaw proved that people want their own infrastructure, keys, data, and model choice, but it leaves the user operating and securing the host.
- Chatticus occupies the missing quadrant: a productized agent organization deployed into the customer's AWS account or attached to local hardware, with models, cost policies, private-system access, reporting lines, and approval gates under customer control.

Required themes:
- Connect to From pair programmer to executive: the human sets direction and defines the organization while agents run the day-to-day loop.
- Connect to The Year Coding Became a Commodity and Maximize Value, Not Intelligence: route each job to the least expensive model that clears the bar, escalate on evidence, and measure accepted outcomes rather than model prestige.
- Explain why model choice is a governance and cost-control decision, not a settings-page nicety.
- Contrast vendor cloud, self-operated hosting, and customer-owned managed infrastructure without caricaturing competitors.
- Explain custom private integrations as part of the deployment boundary; public SaaS connectors remain optional.
- State clearly that Chatticus is under development and do not imply that unshipped capabilities are live.

Publication gate: remain in copywriting/unpublished until the Chatticus launch decision.
payload.title: Chatticus: The AI Organization You Control
